questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go to an English speaking country as well as a university that offered subjects that could be used in some way when returning home. I also wanted to go to a country with a different culture, but not so much that it would be hard to adjust.
I also always wanted to visit Australia, so that was just a plus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university sent out the needed information by email and their website was easy to navigate

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The student information service wasn't very helpful although told to be - they couldn't do anything except tell us to wait and see if the problems would be solved, which was quite stressful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Some colleges as well as student housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
The student associations provided free breakfast most days and free lunch sometimes. Furthermore, said associations provided free meals for students in need and had a little shop where student could shop for "free" (with x amounts of points per week). Also, some of the housing had meals included, but this was quite expensive.
Or else the housing all had cooking facilities, either private kitchens or communal.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is very expensive and if you have the time and patience, I would recommend trying to look into finding housing on my own as you could find it cheaper. However, if you want to avoid the hassle, the housing isn't that bad - of course depending on who you get put together with.
Also be aware, that some of the student housing isn't cleaned very well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Initally it seemed easy. However, many of the courses got removed later on without notification and if you didn't check regurlaly you could end up not having the required amount of courses, when the semester starts. Also be aware that you have to apply for the courses and if given to you, you also have to enroll in said subjects (and some quite fast or else they might get filled up, and you have to find other courses that are not filled up)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. The university had a student information service (Stop 1), but as mentioned they were not very helpful. You kind of had to figure it out own your own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat, some of the courses that I wanted got cancelled, so I had to find new ones, and as a lot of others also cancelled, you were left with very little choice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to check up on your registrered courses  a little while before the semester starts, so you don't end up in a stressed position a few days before the beginning of the semester.
However, don't stress even if you havn't figured out all your courses in the beginning, it will be solved, it might just take time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level is easier than at UPCH, but it doesn't end in one final exam, and you have to turn in assignments or complete quizzes throughout the semester. But id you take BA courses, don't be nervous.
There are also participation marks in some courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching depends on the course, but most of the subjects also have lectures and seminars, so in that aspect it is very much the same. Also the teaching usually consists of the teacher teaching the important elements of the readings and then group work, so similiar to the teaching style in BA courses at UPCH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Principles of Business Law, Corportate Law, IP Law and Legal Language.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you want one les subject in person, PBL is an online tought course.
If you want something very different from what we are used to, Legal Language is the way to go.
If you are interesed in IP, the law in AU is very much the same as in DK.
If you like corporate law, CL might be interesting, but I personally didn't care for it.

Also in general, take BA courses. The rumor is that MA courses are tough, so to make it easier for yourself, why not just apply to BA courses.

questions.answer: Fruit and vegetables were more expensive than expectedk, depending on the sort and the prices also differs from state to state.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UniMelb had lots of different social and athletic clubs plus many social activites.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The surfing club or the skiing club depending on which semester you are there as they arrange both atheltic activities as well as social. 
However, also just taking advantage of the free food available

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit the hiking spots "near" Melbourne, drive down Great Ocean Road and if you have the budget travel around Australia (and New Zealand).
Also just visit all the different suburbs of Melbourne as they are all very different and beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - everyone is friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the social clubs and their events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The peope are very open and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
To pack for colder weather as well if going in the spring semester, as it can get cold close to june.
To budget for trips around Australia.
To take BA courses, make it easier for yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start looking at housing as soon as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met during the semester

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning it is hard being so fr away from home, but soon you start living your life abroad and the home sickness goes away. Just enjoy your time in a new city and with new friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
